flags: minor: distractors A, B, D are far-fetched (quit job, mother's lesson, rescue competition), so the item is very easy
minor: tests nearly the same point as R044-08 (uneventful hours made the rescue possible)
R044-01.notes: Main idea: a guard who never made a rescue sees that her uneventful watching prepared her. Paragraphs 1 and 6 support it directly.

flags: minor: the stem uses the word 'retrieved' for the car-keys sentence, which gives away R044-04 ('fished' = retrieved); see flag on R044-04
R044-02.notes: P1: 'once fished a set of car keys out of the deep end.' D is wrong because training happened in practice and is not retrieving something from the pool; B and C are not in the passage.

flags: minor: 'Mara and others' is a stretch, since only the brother teases her and his teasing implies doubt rather than stating it; still clearly the best choice
minor: the key is the longest choice and the only one that names a purpose
R044-03.notes: P2: the brother's 'Professional sitter' teasing and Mara privately wondering 'what the job was for' set up the rescue and the payoff at dinner. A belongs to P1, C to P3, and B is unsupported.

flags: Cross-item cue: the stem of R044-02 restates the same sentence as 'the only thing Mara had ever retrieved from the pool,' which gives away 'retrieved' as the meaning of 'fished.' The two items also test the same sentence. Revise one of the stems (e.g., change R044-02's wording to 'pulled out of the water' or 'recovered'), or replace this vocabulary item.
R044-04.notes: 'fished ... out of the deep end' = retrieved. A is the literal trap; C and D are weak.

flags: minor: the passage's most direct reason is that the woman 'had not turned around' (she was turned away, laughing with a friend). C is still the best choice because no option mentions distraction, and the silent-drowning theme supports C, but a sharper version would make the stem 'Based on the passage, the boy's distress was easy to miss mainly because:'
R044-05.notes: P3: 'He was not splashing or calling out'; P6: 'The boy had not looked like someone drowning.' D is ruled out because the mother was 'sitting by the fence' (P4), not two yards away. B is wrong because he was in the shallow end near the drop-off rope. A is unsupported.

R044-06.notes: P5: the brother asks 'as usual'; Mara answers 'One' and 'for once he had nothing to add.' The teasing routine ends. B, C and D are unsupported.

flags: minor: purely literal detail item; A ('other guards') is the obvious trap from the same sentence
R044-07.notes: P4: 'His mother ... reached them before the other guards did.' The story is consistent: the mother is not the laughing woman two yards away.

flags: minor: overlaps with R044-01 (same thematic point)
R044-08.notes: P6: 'What had made it possible were the thousands of minutes before it: the ten-second scans of water where nothing happened.' C contradicts 'thousands of minutes' ('a single session'). A and D are not in the passage.

R044-09.notes: Third-person limited ('she remembered', 'she realized'). The other choices are first-person or wrong-character narrators.

R044-10.notes: P4: the contrast with the 'teenagers pretending to struggle' (P1) shows how the real rescue differed from practice. A, B and C are unsupported.
